entries.title: Morgan Park showcases its aerial attack in Payton win
entries.summary: <p>Morgan Park opened the season with challenging road trips to Downers Grove North and Edwardsville and a matchup with Notre Dame. The Mustangs emerged with two wins and a five-point, resume-building loss to ranked Downers North.</p><p>For coach Chris James, the challenge now is keeping his team’s level high in Public League play.</p><p>“I’m not as worried about it as I used to be,” James said. “We do a lot now, as much as we can, to prohibit anything slipping. We used to play bad against teams we should beat, but we are getting better at that.”</p><p>Morgan Park knocked off Payton 61-7 on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/09/10/high-school-football-scores-chicago-illinois" >Saturday</a> at Stagg Stadium.</p><p>The Mustangs ran the ball well over the first three weeks of the season so the focus against Payton was on junior quarterback Ronald Smith Jr. throwing the ball.</p><p>It was a success. Smith was 10-for-13 passing for 221 yards with three touchdowns and one interception.</p><p>He connected with Jeremiah Harvey for a 42-yard TD, Travezz Jones for a 33-yard TD, and Mark Dossous Jr. on an 11-yard score. Jones had four catches for 94 yards.</p><p>“I’m feeling good,” Smith said. “We have been progressing every week. We made a few mistakes the first week and then got better. We still have to improve, though.”</p><p>Senior running back William Smith Jr. opened the scoring with a 72-yard TD run, and Kenneth Sims ripped off a 57-yard TD run in the third quarter.</p><p>Linebacker Raymond Gilbert junior led the defensive effort for Morgan Park (3-1, 1-0 Red Star) with a couple of sacks and a fumble recovery.</p><p>Payton turned the ball over seven times. There were multiple fumbles and several special teams mistakes.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" I don’t blame things on kids. Those are things we will look at on film and get better and come back next week.”</p><p>Payton (3-1, 0-1) scored on an 18-yard pass from Jackson Peters to Zach Hosek late in the first half.</p><p>The Grizzlies opened the season with wins against Corliss, Hyde Park and Amundsen.</p><p>“This is one game, and it does not define our season,” Clark said. “We have a great chance next week against Taft. We are still in the running to go to the state playoffs and the Prep Bowl and all these other great things we can do and play some solid football.”</p><p>Morgan Park’s home base, Gately Stadium, is under construction. Originally, Gately was considered out of commission for the entire season, then there was talk it might reopen halfway through the season.</p><p>“Now [CPS] is saying there is a gate they need on back order, so we won’t be able to play there,” James said.</p><p>This was the first game James has coached at Stagg Stadium. The Mustangs will also play at Rockne and Eckersall this season.</p><p>The long, victorious trip to Edwardsville last week was an eye-opener for the team and excellent preparation for possible road trips in the state playoffs.</p><p>“Edwardsville had an amazing campus,” James said. “That is a very nice place and they have a really solid team.”</p><p>“It is definitely different having to play after a long bus ride,” Morgan Park senior defensive back Darrell Mattison said. “It’s good that we have that experience now.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-c80000" name="html-embed-module-c80000"></a><blockquote class="tiktok-embed" cite="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports/video/7684796062405496094" data-video-id="7684796062405496094" style="max-width: 605px;min-width: 325px;" > <section> <a target="_blank" title="@michaelsobriensports" href="https://www.tiktok.com/@michaelsobriensports?refer=embed">@michaelsobriensports</a> Morgan Park knocked off Payton 61-7. entries.title: Chief Keef Live 2026 Tour concert in Chicago postponed
entries.summary: <p>Saturday was supposed to be a landmark day for Chief Keef fans. </p><p>Fans from Chicago and beyond arrived at Huntington Bank Pavilion at Northerly Island in their best outfits to see the rapper's first show within the city limits in more than a decade.</p><p>As massive groups of spectators lined up in front of the entrance for the Chief Keef Live 2026 Tour kickoff concert, the venue posted a message on its <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/p/DdNISDVj9JS/" target="_blank" >Instagram account</a> around 6 p.m. that the show was delayed. About an hour later, another message appeared saying Keef would not be performing at all. </p><p>"Chief Keef’s September 12th performance at Huntington Bank Pavilion has been postponed," the post read. "All previously purchased tickets will be honored for the new date."</p><p>Neither the venue nor Keef representatives provided a reason for the cancellation. </p><p><i>This is a developing story. Check back with Sun-Times.com for updates. </i> </p>
entries.author: Mark Braboy

entries.title: Will Venable ready to adjust as needed as White Sox try to shake late-season funk
entries.summary: <p>ST. LOUIS, Mo. – With losses in nine of their last 12 games and their division lead shaved down to the bone, the announcement of Saturday’s White Sox lineup seemed to reveal the kind of major shake-up for which the offense’s September struggles had been calling.</p><p>Colson Montgomery and Braden Montgomery–both entering Saturday with an OPS under .600 for the month–were shifted to the bottom two spots of the order. Kyle Teel, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/10/slowed-by-injury-white-sox-catcher-kyle-teel-still-has-tools-for-a-breakout-will-venable-ryan-fuller-bat-speed-chris-getz" target="_blank" ><u>projected preseason to be a middle of the order fixture</u></a> but easing back from an ankle injury, was moved up to second.</p><p>Instead, manager Will Venable defused such notions of a big, reactive change.</p><p>"The change in lineup is not about performance or anything,” Venable said.</p><p>Near the end of Year 2 of the White Sox under Venable’s stewardship, it’s imprudent to assume he’s trying to send a message through the lineup when platoon matchups are the more likely explanation. Sure enough, his expectation that the Cardinals were planning to piggyback right-handed starter Kyle Leahy with left-hander Cooper Hjerpe drove a strategy geared around left-handed bats at the top of the order.</p><p>Of course, with the White Sox fighting for their playoff lives, there’s a world where this order has some staying power.</p><p>“Maybe we score a bunch of runs and we want to keep it exactly the same,” Venable quipped.</p><p>But is there a major adjustment coming as the White Sox suffer through their worst baseball of the season at a decidedly inopportune time? The window for a proactive response to the second half fades of Montgomery, Munetaka Murakami, even spitfire rookie leadoff man Sam Antonacci, has closed. Caleb Bonemer and his 37 minor league home runs could be an intriguing option next year, but there’s no late-season offensive impact waiting for the call in Triple-A Charlotte.</p><p>“We played together all year, the vibes aren’t down,” said Chase Meidroth. “We have to move forward and find a way to win.”</p><p>Hitting coach Derek Shomon is grinding through adjustments in the batting cage, but from a deployment perspective, there’s not many transformative options. Instead Venable has largely kept the faith with his existing core, and his players echo the same steady confidence. What this Sox roster lacks in postseason experience, they make up for in experience in absorbing losses and trusting things will get better.</p><p>“There's been parts of the season where we weren't pitching well, we weren't hitting well, we weren't doing this or we weren't doing that,” Davis Martin told the Sun-Times. “We came out of it every time.”</p><p>“We know things are going to pass and we are going to get back on track when we need to,” said Colson Montgomery.</p><p>The question obviously also extends to the pitching staff, especially where using Sean Newcomb as an opener in front of him did little to stanch <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/11/white-sox-starter-luis-castillo-feels-hes-very-very-close-to-righting-ship-after-working-on-mechanics-colson-montgomery-strikeout-record-chase-meidroth-joey-bart-will-venable" target="_blank" ><u>the bleeding from trade deadline acquisition Luis Castillo</u></a>. Newcomb, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/31/white-sox-sean-newcomb-starter-or-reliever-bullpen-will-venable-grant-taylor-sean-burke-free-agency-chris-getz-rotation-relief" target="_blank" ><u>the heavily-used rock of the bullpen all year long</u></a>, has now been charged with runs in four-straight outings, even though Saturday night was a case of Castillo allowing an inherited run to score, as the right-hander saw his velocity drop into the low-90s, was pulled after less than three innings of work and now has a 7.76 ERA in a White Sox uniform</p><p>The Sox do have starting pitching options in the minors that could be worth exploring, and that could begin as soon as Sunday. Venable contends that if anything, he’s ready to respond to how his players are performing in the moment more than ever.</p><p>“If we’re in early-April, May baseball, you’re kind of spreading out the love, spreading out the opportunity to make sure guys are plugged in,” Venable said. “Now it’s just about one day, and today, and how you’re going to win that game.”</p><p>During this skid, Venable has spent some postgame sessions lamenting moves that haven’t worked out, but insists he’s not hesitant to pull the trigger on some new ones going forward.</p><p>“If there's adjustments that are necessary,” Venable said, “We're going to make them.”<br></p>
entries.author: James Fegan

entries.title: Westinghouse cruises past Curie
entries.summary: <p>Westinghouse missed the IHSA playoffs last year and were dropped from the Public League's top Red division to the second tier this season.</p><p>Neither development sat well with the Warriors, who are aiming to reestablish themselves as an upper-level team in the city.</p><p>"It definitely put a little chip on our shoulder for sure," junior two-way standout Ethan Wiley said.</p><p>Saturday's 42-6 romp past Curie at Rockne Stadium was a step in the right direction.</p><p>Senior Jaidyn Gandy ran nine times for 132 yards — all in the first half — including touchdowns of one and 50 yards. Wiley had five carries for 35 yards and a score. Bernard Mitchell Jr. also had a 50-yard touchdown run.</p><p>Gandy, who also runs track, moved from receiver to running back this season.</p><p>"He's been getting better every week, just working, learning different things," Westinghouse coach Julius Carter said.</p><p>"I love it," Gandy said of the switch. "Just anything to help the team. I know Coach is going to put me in the best possible position to succeed, and I just trust in that."</p><p>He does have previous experience at running back, so the position is not completely foreign to him.</p><p>"We've just got to be a football player at the end of the day," Gandy said.</p><p>Meanwhile, Carter said, "Ethan Wiley is probably one of the best players in the Public League. He's underrated, most definitely."</p><p>Wiley made the All-City team as a sophomore last year.</p><p>"He's a receiver, DB, whatever we need him at," Carter said. "He can do it all — run the ball, he's all-around, just an athlete."</p><p>"I definitely feel like I've got a lot to prove because there's a lot of guys out here [who are] getting way more exposed," Wiley said. "And I know I'm better than them. So yeah, I feel like it's a lot to prove out here."</p><p>Though they're still a win shy of their 2025 total, the Warriors (3-1, 1-0) are IHSA playoff-eligible this season under the expanded postseason format. But they still have a lot to play for in the regular season, even as they are missing some key players who are hurt.</p><p>"We still want to finish strong," Carter said. "The goal was to win conference, make the city and state playoffs and just keep things going in the right direction. So even with the injuries, that's the goal."</p><p>Curie (2-2, 0-1), which was shut out by Lincoln Park last week, also is navigating some injury issues. On Saturday, turnovers were a problem and led to three of Westinghouse's seven touchdowns.</p><p>One bright spot for the Condors was freshman backup quarterback Treyveon Townsend, who had six carries for 33 yards and a TD.</p><p>"I knew these were going to be two tests for us, just being that they were in the [top Red] conference last year," Curie coach Jarve Lewis-Bey said. "But I wasn't expecting this.</p><p>"We knew what they were going to do. They ran the same plays the last three weeks, they ran them this week. We still couldn't stop them."</p>
